basis: Acute inflammatory optic neuropathy, usually immune-mediated; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis.
Scalp aplasia and terminal limb defects define Adams-Oliver syndrome; microcephaly and intellectual disability each occur in 2/6 patients (~33%).
Congenital anatomical anomaly of the inferior vena cava and azygos venous circulation.
Platelet dysfunction and ocular albinism define HPS9; leukopenia and recurrent infections support immune dysfunction (1/1); cutaneous hypopigmentation is a common core feature.
Heterotopic tissue occupies the nose and may obstruct the airway; there is no communication with the CNS.
Inherited defective dental enamel maturation; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Combined dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; cervical muscle contractions do not establish primary muscle disease.
Acquired loss of elastic fibers confined to the papillary dermis; the definition explicitly excludes systemic involvement.
Glycolytic enzyme deficiency causes chronic hemolytic anemia; neurologic impairment and gallbladder complications are under 30%; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
Benign facial adipose tumor, typically in subcutaneous tissue; conjunctival involvement belongs to a specific subtype.
CNS hypomyelination with developmental and motor dysfunction; nystagmus is neurologic, while optic disc pallor occurs in only 1/4 patients.
Congenital humeral trochlear deformity; occasional ulnar nerve palsy does not establish neurologic involvement in at least 30%.
Neurodegenerative parkinsonian syndrome; gaze palsy and abnormal eye movements reflect CNS dysfunction rather than direct eye damage.
Morphine dependence is a substance-use disorder; no intrinsic organ damage is specified.
Nonspecific umbrella rather than an organ-defined disease; no organ or mechanism applies consistently across its heterogeneous subtypes.
Defined by four congenital cardiac abnormalities; the supplied extracardiac HPO features are not characteristic of most patients with isolated tetralogy.
Developmental aortic arch diverticulum; usually asymptomatic, with airway or esophageal compression insufficiently common to add other axes.
SYNJ1-related neurodegenerative parkinsonism; dysphagia, rigidity and gaze abnormalities reflect neurologic dysfunction without demonstrated separate organ injury.
Umbrella explicitly defined by disease of the respiratory system; infection or immune mediation does not apply across the entire group.
Primary trigeminal autonomic headache disorder; tearing, conjunctival redness, ptosis and rhinorrhea are attack-related signs without direct organ damage.
CNS invasion defines sleeping sickness; anemia/splenic involvement and cardiac inflammation with ECG changes are common (~30%+); hepatomegaly alone does not prove liver damage.
Congenital persistence of fetal ocular vasculature with severe vitreoretinal maldevelopment and vision loss in 31/31 patients.
Isolated congenital absence or hypoplasia of the patella; an unspecified skin abnormality lacks evidence of common involvement.
Gastric collagen deposition and inflammation define the disease; autoimmune association does not establish an immune mechanism, and iron-deficiency anemia is separately diagnosed.
Alcohol abuse is a substance-use disorder; alcoholic liver disease and other organ complications are separately diagnosed conditions.
